derivation.conclusion: k_floor <= G holds whenever R + tF >= 0, which is always. The floor is therefore always reachable in principle on this family, and a ratio above one requires reassignment to block every remaining single unit removal before the chain reaches the floor
derivation.decision: D = (1/F) * sum_f (2 g_f - r_f), with g_f the gain and r_f the retained additions
derivation.removable_gain: G = sum_f g_f, since each deletion removes at most one unit of gain
derivation.setting: unit penalties, equal frame weights 1/F over F frames, tolerance t
derivation.step: D*F = 2G - R where R = sum_f r_f, so k_floor = ceil( (2G - R - tF)/2 ) <= G

finding: on this loss and this edit family the fragility ratio is close to tautological, so the two case replication carries much less information than it was presented with
predicted_exception: a ratio above one needs the reassignment structure to exhaust every single unit removal early. The full census is now a test of whether that ever happens, and a census with none is a negative result to report
scope: a statement about the Engine additive loss with unit penalties, equal frame weights and single record deletions. It does not transfer to another loss, another weighting or another edit family without its own derivation
